claim: Using separate accounts for non-production and production separates, by default, the resources and data of one workload environment from other environments and workloads, so each can have its own security and operational controls.
question: Why is a separate production account a stronger isolation boundary than tags and IAM policies in one account?

values.display: separate accounts for the non-production and production environments
by default, the resources and data

evidence.quote: By using separate accounts for the non-production and production environments, by default, the resources and data that make up a workload environment are separated from other environments and workloads.

claim: The Security Tooling (Audit) account provides centralized delegated administrator access to AWS security tools and view-only investigative access into all accounts; it aggregates services such as Security Hub CSPM, GuardDuty, Macie, Firewall Manager, Detective, Inspector and IAM Access Analyzer.
question: Which account holds security tooling, and how are security services delegated?

values.display: centralized delegated admin access to AWS security tooling

qualifiers.scope: Security Tooling account in the Security OU

evidence.quote: In the context of AWS services, this account is used to provide centralized delegated admin access to AWS security tooling and consoles, as well as provide view-only access for investigative purposes into all accounts in the organization.

This account is an aggregation point (or points for organizations that split the functionality across multiple accounts) for AWS security services, including AWS Security Hub CSPM, Amazon GuardDuty, Amazon Macie, AWS AppConfig, AWS Firewall Manager, Amazon Detective, Amazon Inspector, and IAM Access Analyzer.

claim: The identity decision guide says an organization instance of IAM Identity Center helps manage workforce access to AWS accounts: it assigns permissions to users and provisions them to multiple accounts from a central place.
question: Which service grants people access to many accounts, according to the AWS identity decision guide?

values.display: manage your workforce access to AWS accounts
provision the permissions to multiple accounts from a central place

evidence.quote: An organization instance of IAM Identity Center can help you manage your workforce access to AWS accounts as well. It lets you assign permissions to users and provision the permissions to multiple accounts from a central place.

claim: Norstella, formed from a merger of five pharmaceutical solution providers, used AWS Control Tower to build an enterprise multi-account environment and completed its migration in under 5 months, a process that typically takes over 1 year.
question: How did Norstella build an enterprise environment with Control Tower, and how fast?

values.display: used AWS Control Tower to complete its migration

evidence.quote: With support from GlobalLogic, an AWS Partner, Norstella used AWS Control Tower to complete its migration in under 5 months without interrupting business operations. Norstella streamlined the process, which typically takes over 1 year, by participating in the AWS Migration Acceleration Program (AWS MAP), a program for accelerating the cloud migration and modernization journey with an outcome-driven methodology.

When pharma intelligence company Norstella was created from the merger of five pharmaceutical solution providers, it used Amazon Web Services (AWS) to build a scalable enterprise cloud environment from scratch.

claim: Norstella provisions accounts with infrastructure as code instead of involving multiple teams, and when it acquires new businesses it uses AWS Control Tower automation to align their infrastructure.
question: How does Norstella use Control Tower when it acquires a business?

values.display: an infrastructure-as-code approach to provision accounts

evidence.quote: Norstella now uses an infrastructure-as-code approach to provision accounts instead of involving multiple teams.
